title: perf(canary): enhanced auto-detection for latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Improve the performance canary detector to automatically catch small but statistically significant latency and throughput regressions during rollouts and to add conservative rollout guards that prevent full traffic promotion when regressions are detected. This PR implements a multi-tier detection pipeline (baseline aggregation, noise modeling, rolling-window z-score detection) and conservative rollout guard policies (hysteresis, minimum sample size, automated rollback cutoff). Checklist: [x] Add statistical detector service and API endpoints; [x] Extend canary controller with hysteresis and minimum-samples checks; [x] Add configurable thresholds and per-model profiles; [x] Add unit and integration tests for detector; [x] Add dashboard panels and alert rules; [x] Document operational runbook. Changes are backward-compatible defaults; operators can opt-in to stricter thresholds via canary-config. See linked Linear items for acceptance criteria and rollout plan.
commits: Initial detector scaffolding and interface (stat-detector service)
Implement rolling-window latency/throughput aggregation and z-score computation
Add hysteresis logic and minimum-sample enforcement to canary controller
Expose config knobs (sensitivity, window_seconds, min_samples, rollback_cutoff) in canary config schema
Add integration tests: synthetic regression scenarios and rollback validation
Add observability: dashboards, perf-canary metrics, and alert rules
Docs: perf-canary runbook and configuration guide
Fix: reduce flakiness in canary test harness by seeding noise model
review_comments: Sanjay Rao: Nice overall design. A few questions on the noise model - do we use per-model baselines or a global baseline? Also please add a short section in the runbook about how to tune sensitivity for low-traffic models.

Author (Ava Martinez): We compute per-model baselines by default; global fallback when metrics are sparse. Added runbook section and default min_samples=500 to avoid noisy detections for low-traffic models.
Lena Kim: The hystereses looks good but can you explain the semantics of rollback_cutoff vs alert_cutoff in the config? Concerned about oscillation during partial rollouts.

Author: rollback_cutoff is a strict threshold that triggers automated rollback if exceeded for consecutive evaluation windows (configurable count). alert_cutoff only opens an incident without rollback. Added comments and tests to demonstrate non-oscillation with hysteresis enabled.
Diego Alvarez: CI flake observed on integration test in initial run; looks like the synthetic load generator had a race. Please stabilize tests before merge.
Author: Fixed race by adding deterministic seeding and an exponential backoff in the test harness. Re-ran CI locally and updated integration test assertions.
release_notes: Enhanced performance canary: automatic detection of small latency/throughput regressions, conservative rollout guards (hysteresis, min-samples, rollback cutoff), new stat-detector service, config options for sensitivity. No breaking changes by default.
